correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=3,h>=2, the concave discrete sequence g(k)=min(k,h(n-k)) has a strict negative second difference, making its Bernstein expectation strictly concave for 0<p<1; endpoint derivatives force a unique optimum. Binomial reflection at p=1/2 proves positive derivative for n>=3,h>=2, but zero for h=1 or n=2; feasibility S=1-p^n-(1-p)^n uniquely peaks at half. Uniform Lipschitz bounds imply p_n -> h/(h+1) and the claimed linear relative gain for fixed h. For n divisible by h+1, discrete slopes yield exact binomial CDF quantile and the moving-parameter CLT yields the stated positive n^-1/2 displacement. When h>=n-1, g(k)=k for k<n, leading to R=np-np^n, exact p_n=n^-1/(n-1), expected male reserve log n+o(1) and failure 1/n+o(1/n). The embedded standard-library checker passed exact and numerical verification; finite tests are not universal proofs.

value.rationale: The objective mismatch arises directly from two natural finite founding-group questions: maximize expected reproductively active females or maximize the probability the group can mate at all. The theorem establishes sharp parameter boundaries for their incompatibility, and an exact finite binomial-quantile calibration. The fixed-capacity normal correction versus maximally polygynous logarithmic male-reserve scaling are structural differences useful when finite male scarcity matters. Neither the known minimum mating function nor elementary finite enumeration is presented as the contribution.
